title: Expose Quest's --preserve-source-ids/--source-family through lore init --migrate-backlog
description:
User bug report, relayed via opum-agent: 'In lore CLI during lore init I still get alias collision conflicts when migrating from backlog.md to quest.'

Reproduced against real backlog 1.50.1 + quest 0.5.0: a Backlog project with a dotted subtask (task-1.1/task-1.2 under task-1) plus an unrelated plain task-2, migrated into a genuinely empty quest workspace (0 tasks, verified via JSON), fails with 'Alias collision: TASK-2 conflicts with TASK-2', exit 5 -- straight from quest migration backlog apply. Root cause: quest's positional-renumbering allocator flattens the dotted subtasks into fresh sequential ids, and one of those fresh ids happens to land on a string an unrelated, never-dotted task already holds. Quest's own error message already names the fix: --preserve-source-ids --source-family <PREFIX>, and quest's own preview/apply --help document this as deliberate fail-loud behavior (QCLI-155), not a bug to fix on their side.

The actual lore-side gap: neither lore init's flag path nor its interactive wizard exposed a way to reach quest's own documented escape hatch -- grepped the whole source tree, zero hits before this task. An operator hitting this had no way to resolve it without abandoning lore init's flow entirely.

Distinct from quest-cli's own repro (a genuine dual id claim: a live pre-existing quest task colliding with an incoming backlog record) -- confirmed these are two different collision mechanisms via a direct control test (a truly empty quest workspace still collides on MY repro's shape, disproving 'lore populates the workspace first' as an explanation). quest-cli fixed their side's error message to name both causes (QCLI-256); --preserve-source-ids does not help their dual-claim case, only this positional-renumbering case.

acceptanceCriteria.text: --preserve-source-ids and --source-family are exposed as lore init flags, threaded through to Quest's preview and apply calls exactly as Quest's own contract requires (re-supplied identically to both)

Flag-combination validation matches Quest's own pairing requirement: --preserve-source-ids requires --source-family, --source-family only means something with --preserve-source-ids, both require --migrate-backlog

End-to-end verified against the real backlog+quest binaries: the exact repro that reproduced the bug (dotted-subtask flattening colliding with an unrelated plain task id) now migrates successfully with the new flags, and still fails informatively without them
Unit tests cover the option threading through migrateBacklogTasksToQuest (including the crash-resume path) and the adapter's exact argv construction

implementationNotes:
IMPLEMENTED AND VERIFIED (2026-09-09). Threaded QuestBacklogMigrationOptions {preserveSourceIds, sourceFamily} through adapters/quest.ts's preview/apply argv construction, tracker-migration.ts's migrateBacklogTasksToQuest (including the crash-resume apply call), and commands/init.ts's flag parsing/validation/manifest registration. Omitted options build zero extra flags -- the default positional-renumbering path is byte-identical to before this option existed (explicit regression test for this).

End-to-end verified against real binaries, not just unit tests: rebuilt the exact repro from this task's description in a fresh scratch repo. WITHOUT the new flags: identical 'Alias collision: TASK-2 conflicts with TASK-2' exit 5, confirming the baseline still reproduces. WITH --preserve-source-ids --source-family TASK: migration succeeds, exit 0, all 4 tasks land correctly (TASK-1->TASK-1, TASK-2->TASK-2 preserved with no collision, TASK-1.1->TASK-3 and TASK-1.2->TASK-4 with dotted-id aliases intact) -- verified via quest task list --json against the real workspace, not assumed from lore's own output.

Unit coverage: tracker-migration.test.ts (3 new tests: threading through both preview+apply, omitted-options-add-nothing, and the crash-resume path re-supplying options fresh from the current invocation rather than anything persisted) and quest-adapter.test.ts (2 new tests: exact argv shape with flags present, and confirmed absent when omitted). Full suite 2901 pass/1 skip/0 fail, lint/typecheck/lore check all clean.

SEPARATE FINDING, not blocking, filed here for whoever next touches the resume path: while building the clean end-to-end repro, an earlier attempt failed on an unrelated missing-actor-declaration error AFTER preview succeeded (so a pending-migration record was written), and retrying then hit migration_not_found from quest's own status command. Quest's raw response carries error_type:validation for this case, not error_type:not_found -- so migrateBacklogTasksToQuest's existing resume branch (unchanged by this task, cause.type !== not_found) never retries the apply, it re-throws. This predates this task's own change entirely (I only added a parameter to an existing call, not the classification logic) and is a real, narrow crash-resume gap, not something this task's scope covers. Worth its own follow-up if the resume path is ever exercised for real (a genuine process crash between a successful preview and a successful apply, not a failed apply).
